rules.title: Application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: An application screening fee may not exceed the landlord's actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information about the applicant, and in no case may it exceed $30 per applicant. The $30 cap may be adjusted annually in line with increases in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.key_value: thirty dollars ($30) per applicant, adjustable annually commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index beginning January 1, 1998; not greater than actual out-of-pocket costs
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who charge applicants, including guarantors or cosignors, a fee to screen an application to rent residential property.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.interaction_text: This section is not intended to preempt any provisions or regulations that govern the collection of deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not charge an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents charging applicants an application screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Screening process required to charge a fee (first-come or refund)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if it offers either (A) a process that considers completed applications in order received under written screening criteria, approves the first qualified applicant, and charges no fee until the application is actually considered (with refund within seven days of fees inadvertently collected from applications not considered), or (B) a process that returns the entire fee to any applicant not selected, within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of application submission, whichever occurs first.
rules.key_value: refund within 7 days of selecting an applicant or 30 days of submission, whichever occurs first
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents charging applicants an application screening fee.
rules.exemptions: Under option (A), no refund is required to an applicant whose application is denied after consideration for not meeting the landlord's established screening criteria; the landlord may instead offer, at the applicant's discretion, to apply the fee to another rental unit's application.
rules.quoted_span: (2) A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:

rules.title: Itemized receipt for screening fee
rules.requirement: The landlord or agent must give the applicant a receipt for the screening fee, personally or by mail (or by email if agreed), itemizing the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing the applicant's information.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who collect an application screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.

rules.title: Refund of unused screening fee
rules.requirement: If the landlord or agent does not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, it must return to the applicant any part of the screening fee not used for authorized purposes.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who collect an application screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: not perform a personal reference check or does not obtain a consumer credit report, the landlord or their agent shall return any amount of the screening fee that is not used for the purposes authorized by this section to the applicant.

rules.title: Copy of consumer credit report to applicant
rules.requirement: If an applicant paid a screening fee, the landlord or agent must give the applicant a copy of the consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
rules.key_value: within seven (7) days of receiving the report
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who collect an application screening fee and obtain a consumer credit report.
rules.quoted_span: If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
